title: The Curious Case of Trent Alexander-Arnold: From Liverpool Hero to Real Madrid Outcast
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 20, 2026Trent Alexander-Arnold’s move to Real Madrid has not gone to plan. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJust a few weeks after Trent Alexander-Arnold said his goodbyes to Liverpool, he was speaking fluent Spanish at his Real Madrid unveiling.

The boy who grew up on Merseyside, spent 20 years in a red shirt, celebrated every major honor at Anfield and was in line to become captain one day, left everything behind to start a new chapter of his career in the Spanish capital.

There was zero regret on Alexander-Arnold’s face as he stood at the podium in front of reporters, cameras and club president Florentino Pérez, speaking a new language and holding up a white No. 12 shirt. Memorable nights at Anfield were nothing more than a distant memory as he dreamed of epic evenings to come at the Bernabéu.

But fast forward two years and there’s been nothing epic about Alexander-Arnold’s time at Real Madrid. In fact, it’s almost like the player, once heralded as the best right back in the world, dropped off the face of the earth.

Trent Alexander-Arnold played a crucial role in Liverpool’s 2019 Champions League triumph. / Matthias Hangst/Getty Images“He is one of these stories that not a lot of clubs can write, but he is someone people will talk about in 20, 30 and 40 years,” former Liverpool manager Jürgen Klopp said of Alexander-Arnold back in 2024.

The German boss had a front row seat to the fullback’s class during his nine-year stint in the Reds’ dugout. Together, Klopp and Alexander-Arnold won eight trophies, including the 2018–19 Champions League title and the 2019–20 Premier League crown.

Along the way, Alexander-Arnold wrote his own legend with every sensational free kick or diagonal ball that showed off his elite playmaking. The defensive holes in his game were accepted so long as his magical right foot made up for his deficiencies.

Alexander-Arnold was soon named a vice-captain, putting him on the fast track to one day skipper his boyhood club. It just made sense for the Scouser who joined Liverpool at age 6 to eventually lead the team in front of fans that absolutely adored him.

Trent Alexander-Arnold won two Premier League titles with Liverpool. / Steven Halliwell/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesExcept it became increasingly obvious Alexander-Arnold had a different vision for his future. Links to Real Madrid always existed, but they became louder and louder as the 2024–25 season raged on, especially with each day the England international did not sign a contract extension.

Liverpool were romping their way to the Premier League title in Arne Slot’s debut campaign, but there were just as many headlines about Alexander-Arnold’s betrayal than there were about the team’s success. After 20 years and 354 appearances, the homegrown talent was really going to leave Anfield just because he couldn’t ignore the allure of Real Madrid?
Steven Gerrard would never. In fact, he didn’t. But Alexander-Arnold chose a new challenge over his loyalty to Liverpool—and he’s been paying the price ever since.

Trent Alexander-Arnold had a debut season to forget. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid rushed to sign Alexander-Arnold before the 2025 Club World Cup. New boss Xabi Alonso wanted to see his new signing in action as early as possible.
At the time, it was simply a disappointment when Alexander-Arnold missed out on the team’s semifinal clash with Paris Saint-Germain due to injury. But in hindsight, it was a rather large omen.

Alexander-Arnold made just five appearances for Real Madrid in 2025–26 before he suffered a serious hamstring injury in September. He missed over a month’s worth of action, only to soon sustain a muscle tear in December that kept him out until February.
All the while, Real Madrid were floundering. The 15-time European champions saw their La Liga lead disappear, lost the Spanish Super Cup final, fired Alonso and then crashed out of the Copa del Rey.

Even once Alexander-Arnold returned to the pitch, spirits were so down in the Spanish capital that even a return to his best form wouldn’t have meant much. By the end of the season, Real Madrid were trophyless and their blockbuster summer signing had managed just 30 appearances and five assists.

As if things couldn’t get more dire for Alexander-Arnold, he was snubbed by England manager Thomas Tuchel for the 2026 World Cup. The 28-year-old was forced to watch the Three Lions mount a third-place finish on the sport’s biggest stage all while he sat at home, no doubt wondering if things would be different had he just stayed at Liverpool.

Trent Alexander-Arnold (left) is not valued by José Mourinho. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesSuch a lackluster debut campaign and missing the World Cup lit a fire under Alexander-Arnold. It was obvious from the early days of preseason he was hoping to change the narrative in his sophomore season, especially now that Dani Carvajal was no longer standing in his way.

Except new manager José Mourinho had other plans. Just when Alexander-Arnold thought he would be the undisputed starter on Real Madrid’s right flank, the Portuguese boss welcomed Denzel Dumfries to the Bernabéu.
